parsed.why: No trans-specific offence; hate-crime law and police transgender-detainee guidelines exist but enforcement is documented as weak. Anti-trans violence is dated (2001–2014); present signals are social conservatism and police disregard rather than state targeting or universal-exposure measures.

Statute in force since September 2025 jails same-sex conduct two to five years and deports foreign nationals; a trans visitor read under birth sex falls inside it. No recourse, no anti-discrimination, military rule, only an undeveloped enforcement record.

No criminalisation, and courts actively rule for trans people, but recent documented street discrimination, physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans people, and rising political hate speech with death threats, without documented working remedy. Protection outruns policing.

Decriminalised 2022 by a court that read sex discrimination to include gender identity; no documented police, border, custody or violence exposure. But no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, and the social climate is undocumented rather than shown accepting.

No criminalisation since 1791, yet no recognition, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, and a judiciary that does not function as protection. Documented hostility to visibly LGBT people, a 2019 killing, and unresolved advocacy-ban bills.
